cells.quote: Using majority-vote ensemble methods did not cause drastic improvements in scores on either benchmark, with increases from 1% to 5% being observed. We did not observe any model score degradation from using ensemble methods.

result.effect: Nemotron 0.97 vs OSS-20b 0.94; difference statistically significant at middle school, not statistically significant at high school

cells.quote: The differences between the models’ accuracy were not statistically significant using pairwise McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni corrections at the high school level, but they were at the middle school level, with Nemotron scoring significantly better.
cells.note: The study also reports that Nemotron used fewer tokens on average in both benchmarks.

O.outcome_detail: perceived worries for future study and life after school resumption

cells.quote: The association between OSE during school suspension and their WOR after school resumption for girls was signi ﬁcantly stronger (D OSE→WOR = 0.35, p < 0.05) than for boys, controlling for student age.
cells.note: The contrast compares the strength of the OSE→WOR association between girls and boys; no instructional treatment was manipulated.

O.outcome_detail: perceived worries for future study and life after school resumption

cells.quote: OSE was signiﬁcantly associated with perceived WOR both for girls (β = −0.64, p < 0.01) and boys ( β = −0.42, p < 0.01).
cells.note: For girls, higher online learning self-efficacy was associated with fewer perceived worries; this is a measured association, not a causal treatment effect.
